# phenix doctor

<!-- Generated by `make cli-docs` from the phenix command tree. Do not edit. -->

Every command on this page also accepts the [global flags](index.md#options).

## phenix doctor

Check the phenix configuration without a running server

### Synopsis

```text
Check the phenix configuration without a running server

  Prints a header for bug reports (the phenix and minimega versions, OS and
  kernel, user, working directory, the config file read, and whether phenix
  runs in a container), then every setting with its effective value and where
  that value came from (flag, env, config file or default), then each check,
  then a summary that names each failed and warned check, with a hint for
  each failure.

  The checks read the config and users files and report unknown keys, check
  each set environment variable phenix reads (PHENIX_*, PATH, EDITOR,
  SUDO_USER and SUDO_COMMAND) as phenix parses it, warn about PHENIX_*
  variables that name no setting or override a different config file value,
  check the settings every other phenix command refuses or misreads
  (bridge-mode, deploy-mode, log.level and log.system.*), check that the
  store and log files can be written and that the base directories exist,
  check what phenix ui reads at startup (the JWT signing key and lifetime,
  initial users, proxy auth, the TLS key pair and certificate expiry, the
  listen endpoints, and the unix socket's directory and group), and check
  that minimega answers on its socket. --skip takes a check or a group of
  checks; an unknown name fails and lists the valid ones. Secret values,
  such as the JWT signing key and initial users, are redacted. doctor exits
  1 when a check fails, or with --strict when one warns, and 0 otherwise.

  --report adds the hostname to the header and prints the whole output in a
  fenced block to paste into a bug report.

  Like healthcheck, doctor opens no store, unix socket or log file and binds
  no port, so it works while phenix ui is stopped. Run it with the same
  flags, environment and user as the phenix command you are checking.
```

```text
phenix doctor [flags]
```

### Examples

```text
# In the Docker deployment
docker exec phenix phenix doctor

# As JSON, waiting up to 10 seconds for minimega
phenix doctor -o json --timeout 10s

# Without minimega or the settings list, failing on any warning
phenix doctor --skip minimega -x --strict

# Output to paste into a bug report
docker exec phenix phenix doctor --report
```

### Options

```text
  -h, --help                help for doctor
  -x, --no-print-settings   leave out the settings list
  -o, --output string       output format ('text' or 'json') (default "text")
      --report              add the hostname and print the output in a fenced block to paste into a bug report
      --skip strings        checks or groups of checks to skip, comma-separated or repeated (such as minimega or ui.jwt-signing-key)
      --strict              exit 1 when a check warns, not only when one fails
      --timeout duration    how long to wait for minimega to answer (default 3s)
```
